\section{The minimum-spill quadratic form and its exact evaluation}
\label{app:spill}

\subsection{Abstract form}

Let $R:X\to V$ and $B:X\to W$ be linear maps of finite-dimensional real
inner-product spaces.  For $y\in\im R$, define
\[
 h(y)=\min_{Rx=y}\norm{Bx}^2.
\]
The minimum exists: after quotienting the affine fiber by
$\ker R\cap\ker B$, the objective is coercive on a complementary subspace.
If $x_y$ and $x_z$ are minimizers, the polarization of
$\ip{Bx_y}{Bx_z}$ is independent of their choices, because two minimizers for
the same datum differ by a vector whose $B$-image vanishes after orthogonal
projection onto $B(\ker R)^\perp$.  Hence $h$ is a positive semidefinite
quadratic form.  It vanishes precisely when its defining affine fiber meets
$\ker B$.  This proves Proposition~\ref{prop:general-spill}; the automorphism
statement follows by conjugating $R$ and $B$ with the induced isometries.

Equivalently, a minimizing lift and multiplier satisfy the KKT equations
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:kkt-general}
 B^\mathsf TBx=R^\mathsf T\lambda,
 \qquad Rx=y.
\end{equation}
Because the objective is convex and the constraint affine, these equations
are sufficient even when $B^\mathsf TB$ is singular.

\subsection{Rational block certificate}

Write a centered star vector as $y=Zu$ with the matrix $Z$ of
Section~\ref{sec:spill}.  Let $A=A_6/6$ be the rational matrix satisfying
$Ax=u$, and let $B$ select the $210$ external plaquette curvatures.  The exact
solver produces five columns $X$ and multipliers $\Lambda$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:kkt-certificate}
 AX=I_5,
 \qquad B^\mathsf TBX=A^\mathsf T\Lambda.
\end{equation}
It then forms $H=X^\mathsf TB^\mathsf TBX$.  For a canonical link,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:spill-H}
 H=\frac1{7887}
 \begin{pmatrix}
21746&10873&8843&12903&10873\\
10873&21746&8843&10873&12903\\
8843&8843&17686&8843&8843\\
12903&10873&8843&21746&10873\\
10873&12903&8843&10873&21746
 \end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
Direct rational expansion gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:spill-poly}
 \det(\lambda G-H)
 =6\left(\lambda-\frac{37}{33}\right)^3
   \left(\lambda-\frac{391}{239}\right)^2.
\end{equation}
Equations~\eqref{eq:kkt-certificate} prove that $H$ is the minimum cost, not
merely the cost of a trial lift, and \eqref{eq:spill-poly} proves the spectrum.
The same exact calculation succeeds for all eight interior links.

The KKT matrix is singular: its exact rank is $140$.  Floating QR pivoting is
used only to locate a $140\times140$ nonsingular minor.  Fraction-free Bareiss
elimination solves that minor, and substitution into the complete
$220\times220$ integer KKT system verifies every omitted equation exactly.
Thus pivot selection may affect runtime but cannot affect a certified result.
